paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: walking in the truth shows up in how you treat people. The elder had no greater joy than hearing that his children were "walking in the truth" (3 John 1:4). Then he praised Gaius for what he did for the brothers, and especially since they were strangers to him (3 John 1:5). Truth in the head is good, but truth in the hands, the door and the kitchen is what the elder cheered for.

Now look at Diotrephes, who "loves to be first" (3 John 1:9). He refused to welcome the brothers and even put out those who wanted to (3 John 1:10). I think the elder wanted Gaius to see that a heart set on being first has no room left for anybody else. So the elder says, "do not imitate what is evil, but what is good" (3 John 1:11). Friend, I've been the stamper nobody made room for, so I know how much a welcome matters.

So who do you copy, baker? The elder says supporting people who go out for the Name makes us "fellow workers for the truth" (3 John 1:8). That means every cup of coffee, every spare bed and every kind word counts as real work. Pick a Gaius to follow, or a Demetrius with a good testimony (3 John 1:12), and open your door wide. That's a batch worth baking.
